sections.heading: 1. Wall leg lift
lines: ① Lie on your side, back and heels to a wall.
② Bend your knees slightly, hips stacked.
③ Lift the top leg, heel on the wall.
④ 10 slow lifts, then switch sides.

caption:
Momo spends half of Pilates class lying on her side, lifting one leg up and down. Is it actually doing anything?

The side-lying series trains the muscles on the outside of your hip, the ones that keep your pelvis level when you walk, run or climb stairs. Lying down means little load through the knees or lower back.

The secret is control, not height. Try it with your back and heels against a wall: 10 slow lifts, heel touching the wall. If lying on your side is uncomfortable, a towel or pillow often helps. Ongoing side-of-hip pain is worth an assessment.

Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio can guide you. Book online via the link in bio.
